figure: Figure 3.4 — Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior

Verify: 1.4 + 5.7 + 5.7 = 12.8B → 25.6 GB; 8 × 5.7B + 1.4B = 47.0B → 94 GB; 68 + 22.8 + 2.8 = 93.6 GB ≈ 94 GB.

figure: FIGURE 3.4 — KV comparison boxes ('dense 12 GB vs MoE 0.6 GB')
issue: The KV comparison is not reproducible from the shape labels printed beside it. A reader who recomputes from '32L/4096H GQA' gets a 5× ratio, not the 20× that the drawn totals imply, so the figure invites a false inference about how much of the KV saving comes from GQA versus from layer count.
evidence: Drawn: 'dense 12 GB vs MoE 0.6 GB' with '8-bit KV set by shape, not routing: 80L/8192H MHA vs 32L/4096H GQA'. Dense: 2 × 80 × 8192 × 1 B = 1.31 MB/token → 12.05 GB at 9,200 tokens (consistent with the house 8-bit KV figure of ~1.31 MB/token). MoE from the printed shape: 2 × 32 × 4096 × 1 B = 0.262 MB/token → 2.41 GB at 9,200 tokens, i.e. 5× dense, not 0.6 GB. 0.6 GB is reachable only with 8 KV heads × 128 head-dim (2 × 32 × 8 × 128 × 1 B = 0.0655 MB/token → 0.60 GB), a fact the figure never states.
acceptance_test: Add the KV-head count and head dimension to the shape label (e.g. '32L/4096H, 8 KV heads × 128') and state the context length both totals assume (9,200 tokens), so that 12 GB / 0.6 GB = 20× is derivable from the printed text; otherwise recompute and redraw the two totals.
